  1. Taking a snapshot at transaction start

  3. At commit time, checking if there are conflicts (write-skew) with other transactions

- In contrast, databases like Oracle or SQL Server implement SERIALIZABLE by locking all rows read (using shared locks that block other transactions from modifying those rows).
